_what: Policy scan rules for the QA gate (stand-in for SOP 6.2 until the SOP arrives). spec/QA-policy.md is generated from this file: edit here, then run python3 engines/policy_scan.py --write-policy.

_sources.policy_safe: Launchpad Ads: Policy-Safe One-Pagers (Andy's Drive, 2026-10-16), red-flag words table, built from Meta Advertising Standards and FTC guidance
_sources.brief: spec/ad-editor-brief.md (DLT Ad Editor Brief), Chapter 04 Words / Footage
_sources.rule4: Andy operating rule 4: never put a number on screen that was not spoken in that video

severity.BLOCK: Cannot ship. Fix the words or the footage, then re-render.
severity.HOLD: Ships only after Andy accepts it in writing (plans/<ad>/acceptances.json, his exact words).
severity.NOTE: Worth knowing; never stops a render.

rules.why: Promise of income. Meta bans promises of financial gain; the FTC needs written proof, dates and the share of buyers who got that result.
rules.instead: Describe what they get (ads, scripts, follow-up), not the money.

rules.why: Guarantee of financial gain: banned by Meta.
rules.instead: "If you do the work and miss the goal we set together, we keep going at no extra cost."

rules.why: A results guarantee (jobs, not money). Allowed in principle, but the terms (what 'booked' means, the conditions) must be written on the landing page, which Meta reviews with the ad.
rules.instead: Keep it, with the terms on the page; or 'If I don't book you the jobs, you don't pay.'

rules.why: One of Meta's own examples of a banned income ad.
rules.instead: "Add a high-ticket service", "start a business with support".

rules.why: Meta bans claims that little or no work is needed to make money.
Close to 'runs without you': can read as little or no work needed. Lower risk when it describes the lead flow, not the money.
rules.instead: "Jobs coming in every week", "we follow up with every lead for you".
"Your ads can start in your first week" (only if true).

rules.why: Implies the ad knows the viewer's financial situation (Meta personal-attributes rule).
rules.instead: Name the trade, not their money: "Exterior cleaners who want more booked jobs."

rules.why: A money figure on screen can read as an income claim (Meta reviews what is shown, not only what is said).
rules.instead: Show the trade or the job count instead of a dollar figure.

rules.why: An earnings claim through someone else's mouth is still an earnings claim; the FTC wants the typical result.
rules.instead: Testimonial about the experience, no dollar amounts.

rules.why: Sensational, low-quality text gets rejected. (All-caps on-screen titles are the brief's style; this rule is about '!!!', WARNING, BREAKING.)
Making Facebook/Instagram the focus or naming other brands breaks brand and trademark rules.
Profanity is banned in ads, even masked; Meta can limit delivery.

manual.check: No bank/payout screenshots, cash or luxury cars on screen (money and lifestyle visuals read as income proof).
Testimonials are real people in their own words; anything they got for it is disclosed on screen.
The landing page and form were reviewed too: Meta checks the ad, page and form together.
Footage: outdoors, real over stock; no offices, desks, cars or white walls; never a person on a ladder with a buzzing phone.
Watched once on a real phone, sound on and off.
